{{Short description|Decomposable function in cryptography}}
[[File:AES-SubBytes.svg|thumb|The SubBytes transformation of the [[Advanced Encryption Standard]] is a notable{{sfn|Weinmann|2009|p=36}} example of a bricklayer function: each 8-bit bundle of the 128-bit state is undergoing the same [[S-box]] transformation independently]]
In [[cryptography]], the '''bricklayer function''' is a part of a [[Round (cryptography)|round function]] that can be decomposed into identical independent Boolean operations on the partitioned pieces of its input data,{{sfn|Daemen|Rijmen|2013|p=22}} so called '''bundles'''.{{sfn|Daemen|Rijmen|2013|p=20}} The term was introduced by [[Joan Daemen|Daemen]] and [[Vincent Rijmen|Rijmen]] in 2001.{{sfn|Weinmann|2009|p=36}}

If the underlying function transforming the bundle is nonlinear, it is traditionally called an [[S-box]]. If the function is linear, Daemen and Rijmen use for it the term '''D-box''' (after [[Confusion and diffusion|'''d'''iffusion]]).{{sfn|Daemen|Rijmen|2013|p=22}}
